summary: This document defines a YANG data model to configure and manage the IS-IS routing protocol on network elements.

eli5.summary: IS-IS is another way routers share maps. This document defines a common form for setting it up and checking on it.

questions: what is the ietf-isis yang module
how do i configure is-is with yang
what notifications does the is-is yang model define
what are level-1 and level-2 in is-is configuration
subtitle: A standard YANG data model for configuring IS-IS routers and reading their state, built to be extended by vendors.

tldr.problem: Operators need one common way to configure the IS-IS routing protocol and read its operational state across equipment from different vendors.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-isis YANG module augments the generic routing model from RFC 8349 with an isis container for configuration and read-only state, adds two RPCs and a set of notifications, and reuses modules for interfaces, key chains and BFD.
tldr.outcome: It gives a vendor-neutral baseline that vendors are expected to extend, and it is designed for the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA). Its write access, state data and RPCs all need protecting.

today: RFC 9130 is a Proposed Standard from October 2022, and nothing in the metadata marks it as obsoleted or updated. IANA registered the module name ietf-isis and its namespace URI.

sections.title: What the Module Covers
sections.content:
RFC 9130 defines a YANG data model (RFC 7950) for the IS-IS routing protocol. The model covers the configuration of an IS-IS protocol instance and the retrieval of IS-IS operational state. Tree diagrams follow the notation of RFC 8340.

The module is designed for the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342. It is intended to be managed by protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF, and the module itself says it holds the generic configuration and state common to all vendor implementations, to be extended by vendors with things like route policies.
sections.eli5: It is a standard order form for setting up and checking an IS-IS router, so every maker's router can read the same form.

sections.title: How the Model Is Organized
sections.content:
The module augments the control-plane-protocol list in the ietf-routing module of RFC 8349 with an isis container. Configuration has two areas: global parameters, such as lsp-mtu, lsp-lifetime, lsp-refresh and default-metric, and per-interface settings. Further modules that add parameters MUST augment ietf-isis.

Many capabilities are optional features. For example, admin-control lets a client shut down one IS-IS instance, and a device that advertises the feature tells the client it supports that.

The model also supports Multi-Topology IS-IS (RFC 5120). A topologies container enables it, and each topology name should refer to an existing RIB of the device. Several address families can also be enabled in the default topology through the address-families container, which needs the nlpid-control feature.

Other pieces include IGP/LDP synchronization (RFC 5443) through an ldp-igp-sync feature, an ISO clns-mtu parameter added to interfaces, and IP Fast Reroute with Loop-Free Alternates (RFC 5286) and remote LFAs (RFC 7490). Remote LFAs cannot be enabled unless LFAs are enabled. The candidate-enabled leaf marks an interface as usable as a backup.
sections.eli5: The form has a section for the whole router and a section for each network plug. Fancy options are optional extras, and a router says which extras it has.

sections.title: Per-Level and Per-Interface Settings
sections.content:
IS-IS has two levels, and many parameters can be set per level. Such a parameter is modeled as a container with three places to set it: a top-level container that applies to both levels, a level-1 container and a level-2 container.

An implementation MUST prefer a level-specific value over a top-level one. In the RFC's example, a priority of 100 for level 1 and 250 at the top level means level 1 uses 100 and level 2 uses 250. Likewise, an interface-specific parameter MUST be preferred over a global IS-IS parameter.

Some parameters, such as the overload bit and route preference, are not modeled per level. An implementation that supports them per level MUST augment the model with both level containers and reuse the existing groupings. An implementation that cannot support per-level configuration, or that lacks the top-level form, should advertise a deviation.

Each interface in the module is a reference to an interface in the ietf-interfaces module (RFC 8343). Interface settings include hello-interval, hello-multiplier, priority, metric, passive, csnp-interval, interface-type, BFD settings and fast-reroute options.
sections.eli5: You can write one rule for the whole school, or a different rule for just one grade. The grade's rule wins, and a rule for one classroom beats both.

sections.title: Authentication Parameters
sections.content:
Authentication is configured through the ietf-key-chain module (RFC 8177), whose groupings the IS-IS module reuses for global and per-interface settings. An authentication type can be either a key-chain reference or a direct key with a crypto-algorithm.

If global authentication is configured, an implementation SHOULD authenticate PSNPs, CSNPs and LSPs with the supplied parameters. Authentication of Hello PDUs can be turned on per interface.
sections.eli5: Routers can use a secret password, or a list of passwords that change over time, so they only talk to friends.

sections.title: Operational State
sections.content:
The read-only state is split into containers. system-counters holds statistics about the whole system. adjacencies shows current IS-IS adjacencies. database shows the contents of the Link State Database (LSDB), local-rib shows the IS-IS internal routing table, hostnames maps system IDs to hostnames (RFC 5301) and there is also IP FRR state.

spf-log records Shortest Path First events and lsp-log records LSP events such as receiving an LSP or changing a local one. Both SHOULD be implemented as wrapping buffers, and an implementation MAY also log LSP refreshes.

Each interface also has event counters, such as adjacency-changes and authentication-fails, and packet counters in and out for IIH, ISH, ESH, LSP, PSNP and CSNP PDUs.
sections.eli5: Besides the order form, the router keeps a diary and a scoreboard. They show who its neighbors are, what happened, and how many messages it sent and received.

sections.title: RPCs and Notifications
sections.content:
The module defines two RPC operations. clear-database resets the contents of an IS-IS database and restarts database synchronization with all neighbors. clear-adjacency restarts a chosen set of IS-IS adjacencies.

It also defines a long list of notifications, including database-overload, lsp-too-large, if-state-change, adjacency-state-change, authentication-failure, area-mismatch, rejected-adjacency, lsp-received and lsp-generation. Most fire on a specific event, such as receiving a PDU with the wrong authentication information or a Hello from an IS that shares no area address.
sections.eli5: The router can ring a bell when something odd happens. There are also two reset buttons: one to redo its neighbor friendships and one to redo its map.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is accessed through management protocols such as NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF. Access can be restricted with the Network Configuration Access Control Model (RFC 8341).

The writable subtrees /isis and /isis/interfaces/interface[name] are sensitive. Changing IS-IS configuration can compromise the entire IS-IS domain, for example by forming adjacencies with unauthorized routers or by making an interface cost asymmetric so a hard routing loop results.

The readable subtrees /isis/database and /isis/local-rib expose the detailed topology of the network, which operators may consider confidential. The clear-adjacency and clear-database RPCs can be used for denial of service. Authentication key data is sensitive, because compromise would let an attacker forge IS-IS traffic that is accepted as authentic. Implementations must rate-limit notifications to avoid a heavy notification load.
sections.eli5: Whoever can change the router's settings can mess up the whole neighborhood, and whoever can read its maps learns the layout. So only trusted people should get in.

items.title: Interface over global
items.text: An interface-specific parameter MUST be preferred over a global one.

items.title: Level over top level
items.text: A level-1 or level-2 value MUST be preferred over the top-level value.

items.title: Top level
items.text: Applies to both levels when no level value is set.
